newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SOCCER-HONG KONG PLANS HANDOVER EXTRAVAGANZA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HONG KONG PLANS HANDOVER EXTRAVAGANZA.

text.p: Already in the throes of "handover" fever, Hong Kong has been promised yet another once-in-a-lifetime treat to commemorate its return to China -- a "Reunification Cup" all-star football extravaganza.

Football officials from FIFA, the sport's international governing body, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and the Hong Kong Football Association on Friday announced a July 3 game between a FIFA all-star team and an AFC all-star team.
The FIFA all-star team will include Liberia's George Weah, world player of the year in 1996, and England's Alan Shearer, top scorer in the Euro'96 tournament.

"As far as sport is concerned, nothing means more to the lives of millions of people in Hong Kong than soccer," Timothy Fok, executive vice president of Sport Community for Celebration of Reunification of Hong Kong with China, told a news conference.
"And for millions more in Hong Kong, nothing means more to them than the reunification with China later this year."
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight of June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule.
The handover will be marked by much fanfare as Britain returns the colony to China, and officials have been casting about for opportunities to mark the event with maximum fanfare.

Apart from a fanatical devotion to horse-racing -- and the annual Rugby Sevens which attracts more westerners than local Chinese -- the business-loving territory generally has little time for sport, but the local soccer league with seven first division teams does draw its share of avid vans.
The FIFA all-stars/AFC all-stars will feature some of the cream of world football, to make for a special game, the game's organisers promised.
Fok said it would be "without doubt the most exciting sports fixture that this territory has ever staged".
"Football is a sport which directly and indirectly touches a fifth of the world's population," FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter said.
Those football-lovers hoping for an annual tournament will be disappointed -- it is a one-off clash after which the trophy will remain in Hong Kong as a "reunification memento".
